🔻 Iranian, Turkish presidents stress deeper bilateral, regional cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian and his Turkish counterpart, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, have underscored the need to deepen bilateral ties and expand regional cooperation, particularly in the political, economic, and trade sectors.

The two presidents held talks on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Turkiye, discussing ways to strengthen relations and the latest regional and international developments, the Iranian president’s office said on Thursday.
​
Emphasizing the historical, cultural, and civilizational ties between the two neighboring countries, Pezeshkian and Erdogan called for making better use of their extensive capacities to expand cooperation in various fields.
​
They also highlighted the importance of boosting trade, facilitating economic cooperation, strengthening private-sector engagement and exploring new opportunities for cooperation between Tehran and Ankara.
​
The two leaders further exchanged views on regional developments, stressing the need for closer cooperation among regional countries to safeguard peace, stability and lasting security.
​
They underlined the need for dialogue, constructive engagement, and joint efforts to prevent escalating tensions and spreading insecurity across the region, highlighting the shared responsibility of regional countries to address common challenges through cooperation and convergence.

💬 Effective environmental programs depend on regional security and stability: Environment Department chief

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Head of the Department of Environment Shina Ansari says implementing effective environmental programs depends on security and stability in the region, highlighting the environmental consequences of recent wars against Iran.

Speaking on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, on Thursday, Ansari made the remarks during a meeting with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz.
​
According to a statement by the Department of Environment, Ansari underlined the damaging effects of the wars on Iran’s environment, particularly explosions at fuel storage facilities and the resulting pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
​
She also thanked the Turkish government for its position regarding the two imposed wars and stressed the need for regional security and stability to enable effective environmental action.
​
Yilmaz, for his part, pointed to longstanding cultural ties between the two countries and said Turkiye was ready to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including environmental protection.
​
Referring to the activation of the joint environmental committee following last year’s Zero Waste Summit, he stressed the importance of continued cooperation in protecting natural resources and habitats.
​
He added that both countries would pursue their shared responsibilities in combating climate change alongside regional issues.
